name: Siter.io
tagline: Visual website design and publishing with Figma import and collaboration

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10 pages and 3 forms; pricing page displays unlimited websites and teammates, with Figma plugin and SSL
tiers.notes: The page's free-plan wording is unusually broad; custom-domain and published-site restrictions are not numerically explained there.

tiers.name: Solo
tiers.limits: 1 website, 2 editors included, 10 pages, 3 forms, Figma plugin and SSL
tiers.notes: Annual billing exists, but its current numeric effective price was not exposed by the accessible pricing HTML.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 3 websites, 4 editors included, 50 pages, 5 forms, Figma plugin and SSL
tiers.notes: Annual price not exposed in accessible first-party HTML.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 5 websites, 6 editors included, unlimited pages and forms, Figma plugin and SSL
tiers.notes: Annual price not exposed in accessible first-party HTML.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 pages and 3 forms; the live table labels websites and teammates unlimited, but does not clearly state publication/domain limits
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; exact annual prices not exposed in accessible first-party HTML
pricing.hiddenCosts: Additional websites and teammates beyond a paid plan's allowance are billed monthly, but the public help page does not publish their unit prices.

verdictSummary: The visible collaborative website builder loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Siter.io earns its keep through editor, CMS, hosting, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused collaborative website builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Siter.io: A single site is easy to code. People pay for safe ongoing edits, templates, publishing, domains, collaboration, and no-maintenance hosting.
ongoingBurden: Maintain responsive rendering, browser compatibility, deployment, domains, forms, spam protection, backups, and editor migrations.

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: A collaborative visual builder with Figma import, hosting and custom domains on the free plan; the badge stays.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: An editor framework with no finished collaboration, import and publishing product.

rejectedAlternatives.name: TeleportHQ
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Figma import looks promising until the current seven-day editor trial ends.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Siter.io is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Siter.io, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a focused collaborative website builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: general-purpose visual editing; large template and component libraries; CMS collaboration and client handoff.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
